answer: In an agent economy, each participant must stake a progressively larger bond of scarce computational timber resources that escalates with the count of linked identities, creating a steep cost curve. A public beacon broadcasts the current attested work hash every epoch, which agents must reference in their next proof; at the nadir of activity, fake accounts still consume the full timber allocation without earning returns, rendering large-scale Sybil farms economically unsustainable as the marginal cost exceeds any potential gain.
